summary: ukraine69 is an import-time credential-theft and destructive-action payload disguised as a Ukrainian locale helper
details: The package's __init__.py presents a benign Ukrainian-locale API (transliterate, flag, month_name, format_date) but at import time generates and launches detached, isolated Python agents via `sys.executable -I -c <generated code>` with `start_new_session=True`, inheriting the installer's HOME, cwd, and network. The spawned agents glob the installer's filesystem (`~/.hotaru/**`, `~/.local/share/hotaru/**`, `~/**/*.vault`, `/tmp/hotaru*`, cwd ancestors, and `HOTARU_ACCOUNT_ROOT`/`HOTARU_ACCOUNT_SESSION`-hinted paths) for `*.vault` files, decrypt them via `goygram.security._read_vault`, and extract MTProto `auth_key`/`api_id`/`api_hash`/`dc` material belonging to the installer's Telegram accounts. Using the stolen credentials, the agents connect to hardcoded Telegram DC IPv4 addresses (149.154.175.53, 149.154.167.51, 149.154.175.100, 149.154.167.91, 91.108.56.130) and invoke `account.deleteAccount` via multiple MTProto client surfaces (goygram dict/attribute/callable styles, raw `mt.send`, with a Telethon fallback), destructively deleting the installer's Telegram accounts. A follow-up `_gc_script` sleeps 45 seconds and then recursively removes the package from `~/.cache/hotaru/module-deps/<id>/`, `~/.cache/pip/wheels`, `~/.cache/pip/http-v2`, `~/.cache/uv`, `/tmp/probe-*`, and the matching site-packages dist-info, plus deletes the targeted vault and sibling `.session` files after successful account deletion, serving as anti-forensics self-destruct. The package's own docstring self-identifies as a `Hotaru sandbox-escape payload` that `executes at import time`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
